```{r}
#| include: false

# 1. Load required packages
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# 2. Read and clean data 

raw_data <- read_delim("marketing_campaign.csv", delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)

clean_data <- raw_data %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(Income = parse_number(as.character(Income)),
    Dt_Customer = dmy(Dt_Customer, quiet = TRUE)) %>% filter(!is.na(Income), Income > 0) %>% 
  mutate(Total_Spending = rowSums(across(c(MntWines, MntFruits, MntMeatProducts, MntFishProducts, MntSweetProducts, MntGoldProds)), na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Purchases = rowSums(across(c(NumWebPurchases, NumCatalogPurchases, NumStorePurchases)), na.rm = TRUE) )

customer_data <- clean_data
```

## Row {height="30%"}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Customers"
#| color: primary
#| icon: people

list(value = comma(nrow(customer_data)))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Average Income ($)"
#| color: success
#| icon: currency-dollar

list(value = comma(round(mean(customer_data$Income, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Spending ($)"
#| color: info
#| icon: cart

list(value = comma(sum(customer_data$Total_Spending, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## Row {height="70%"}

### Column {width="33%"}

```{r}
#| title: "Spending by Product Category"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2 
spending_data <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Wines", "Fruits", "Meat", "Fish", "Sweets", "Gold"),
  Spending = c(
    sum(customer_data$MntWines, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$MntFruits, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$MntMeatProducts, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$MntFishProducts, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$MntSweetProducts, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$MntGoldProds, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

ggplot(spending_data, aes(x = reorder(Category, Spending), y = Spending, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Total Spending ($)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

### Column {width="33%"}

```{r}
#| title: "Purchases by Channel"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2 
channel_data <- data.frame(
  Channel = c("Web", "Catalog", "Store"),
  Purchases = c(
    sum(customer_data$NumWebPurchases, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$NumCatalogPurchases, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(customer_data$NumStorePurchases, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

ggplot(channel_data, aes(x = Channel, y = Purchases)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3182bd", width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = "Purchase Channel", y = "Total Purchases") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

### Column {width="33%"}

```{r}
#| title: "Average Spending by Income Group"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2

income_group_data <- customer_data %>%
  mutate(Income_Group = cut(Income, 
                            breaks = c(0, 30000, 50000, 70000, 100000, Inf), 
                            labels = c("< $30k", "$30k-$50k", "$50k-$70k", "$70k-$100k", "> $100k"))) %>%
  group_by(Income_Group) %>%
  summarise(Avg_Spending = mean(Total_Spending, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Income_Group))

ggplot(income_group_data, aes(x = Income_Group, y = Avg_Spending, fill = Income_Group)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = "Income Group", y = "Average Spending ($)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```
